title: Uniform rounded prime-power cyclic inversion (no κ claim)
body:
Supplies a rounded inverse for the prime-power cyclic kernels of PR621. Stable first-order factors use two scans, including the periodic closure. The full neighboring-shift inverse uses `O(r)` array passes and `p+O(r^4)` precision, independent of cyclic length. The proof charges approximate factor preparation, coefficient verification and unit-phase approximation. The extension to independently varying unit phases at every position has the same length-independent precision bound, with every phase oracle charged.

The standard bit-model bound is `soft-O((Lr+r^3)(p+r^4))`. Its preparation argument uses the cited Pan factorization and fast elementary-function algorithms. The reference root finder only nominates candidates; exact coefficient enclosures, factor products and rounding budgets certify them. Those worst-case preparation algorithms are not implemented here.

A separate inverse-shear construction now restores the source and `ceil(log2(r-1))` borrowed dirty arrays exactly. Causal integer lifts implement each stable factor; balanced commutators compose them. It uses `O(r^2)` factor calls and `O(p+log(D+1)+r^5)` precision for initial magnitude bound `D`, independent of cyclic length. It permits charged clean scalar arithmetic and read-only phase access; reversible bit arithmetic and a common-label word are not supplied. The rounded target increment may depend on the initial dirt within the proved error bound.

Arbitrary strides have an explicit two-sort reduction, with `O(L(B+log L)log L)` routing cost. That can become `O(Lp^2)`, so the package exposes the remaining layout requirement. Scheduling the borrowed arrays in the complete transform, full-transform composition, normalization, bit compilation and the multiplication reduction remain open. **No new integer κ, complex b, BIT c, practical speedup or literature-priority claim.**

Validation:

- Fresh macOS/Python 3.14 and Linux aarch64/Python 3.12 replays passed in 164.74s and 163.67s. All nine deterministic certificates are byte-identical across platforms.
- 108 generic scan cases; 480 mixed-factor cases, including 240 independent dense solves; 345 precision-budget cases; 8384 stride mappings and 43 routed executions; 116 varying-coefficient/phase cases with 72 additional dense comparisons; 36 dirty-factor cases, 120 dense dirty compositions, 24 actual-kernel dirty cases, 1035 dirty precision budgets; 48 rejection controls, including eight instruction mutations.
- Ten kernel/embedding certificates through radix 16 cover inner and outer factors, exact rational phases and a certified approximation of `exp(2πi/7)`, each with an all-length `2^-128` error bound.
- Complete receipts, stage logs and hash verification are included. Every staged blob was checked against the source/evidence manifests. A Python 3.11/3.14 CI workflow replays the package.

The package is standalone and uses the Python standard library. Kernel, mathematical-source and substantial OpenAI Codex assistance credits are recorded in `NOTICE.md` and `SOURCE.json`.
